Banks and ABC need the filed FBN statement.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File the Place of Entertainment permit application with the SF Entertainment Commission, including the lease, BAN, and a description of the entertainment (type, hours, sound equipment). What to say: Email the Deputy Director at the Entertainment Commission to confirm eligibility before applying. File the application online with the $2,708 fee (2026–27 schedule). The Commission will refer it to Police, Planning, DBI, DPH and Fire for review. Post a yellow notice at the premises for 30 days and conduct neighbor outreach as instructed. State that the entertainment is live performance in an existing bar, that soundproofing will contain bass and vibrations per the CUA conditions, and that a community liaison and patron behavior notices will be in place. The Commission holds a public hearing (1st and 3rd Tuesdays) approximately 3–4 months after filing; approval is by motion. Do not file the POE application until after the Planning Commission approves the CUA, so that the Planning referral response can reference the CUA approval.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File the DPH plan check for the kitchen (if remodeling) and apply for the health permit to operate, with proof of a certified food safety manager and a seller's permit. What to say: Submit kitchen plans, equipment specs, finishes and the menu to DPH online or at 49 South Van Ness. The 2026–27 plan check fee is $828 (small remodel, 3 hrs) to $2,207 (new restaurant, 8 hrs). One owner or employee must pass an accredited food safety certification exam (ServSafe or equivalent, $100–$250) within 60 days of opening. After plan approval, schedule a pre-final inspection at ~80% complete and a final inspection at least two weeks in advance. The health permit to operate ($470 application fee, $0 annual license for bars/restaurants in 2026–28) is issued after the final inspection confirms the facility matches the approved plans and the certified manager is on staff. Do not serve food to the public before the permit is issued.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $3,800 to $18,000. Notes: The day range is the time to obtain the discretionary approvals when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days from filing to approval per the catalog and the one comparable with a filing date, which took 538 days but is an outlier) and Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days per the catalog). The building permit (14–120 days per the catalog) and health permit (14–45 days) follow approval of the CUA and are not discretionary hearings, so their time is not the long pole. Cost range covers the CUA application fee (~$3,150 CPI-adjusted), the POE application fee ($2,708 in 2026–27), the building permit ($800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation for soundproofing and tenant improvements), and the health plan check and permit ($828–$2,207 plan check, $470 permit application). The total does not include the acoustic consultant's fee (likely $2,000–$5,000 for a report and soundproofing plan), the architect's fee for building permit plans (typically $5,000–$15,000 for a bar/entertainment remodel), or construction costs (soundproofing, finishes, equipment). These are professional service and construction costs, not government permit fees, so they are not in the range above. The CUA is the critical path: 4–10 months including pre-application meeting, filing, environmental review, neighborhood notice, hearing scheduling and the 30-day appeal period. File it immediately after the entity is formed and the BAN is obtained. The POE application should be filed after the CUA is approved so that the Planning referral can reference the CUA approval.
